keyframe_review.note: 6,727 km2, Scania in southern Sweden (12.6-14.3 E, 55.4-56.1 N), 480-489. This is the Origo's legend, not a place the page puts the Lombards in the 480s: 'The Origo and the History of Paul the Deacon have them first living on an island in the far north'. The Lombards page, re-read 2026-10-20, puts them elsewhere: 'They had previously settled in the Middle Danube in the 5th century, near what is now Austria, Slovenia and Hungary' and 'They reappear in historical records living near the Danube river in the late 5th century'; the only dated stop is Rugiland, where they arrived 'after 487'. The correction draws the Middle Danube for 480-487 as a 110 km circle round Szombathely, where the three countries meet (about 38,000 km2; confidence 1, a bridging reading: the page gives the 5th century, not the years). It replaces the first draft's Bardowick, the 1st-century homeland the page gives only through place-names ('near the first known homeland of the Langobardi'). No area on the page for a comparison.

Sirmium ... since 536, after taking it from the Byzantine emperor Justinian I' until the Gepid king 'handed Sirmium over to the Byzantines' (Cunimund died 567). region.text: Rugiland, the Rugian territory north of the Danube in Lower Austria, 'subsequently settled by the Lombards'

ledger.note: 488: the Lombards settle Rugiland. They 'arrived after 487 when Odoacer defeated the kingdom of the Rugii' (Lombards page: 'defeat in 487/488 AD of the Rugii'); the Heruli page has 'the Lombards moved and occupied their country, and they stayed there a number of years' under 488, and the Odoacer page, read 2026-10-20, has 'the abandoned province was settled by the Lombards by 493'; the Rugiland page: the territory 'was subsequently settled by the Lombards'. The year 488 is the first after the page's 487, within the Odoacer page's 'by 493' (confidence 2: the region is the Rugiland reading). The counterpart is Odoacer, who took the Rugian land in 487-488; his dossier (eu-04) keeps Rugiland in its 488-493 keyframe with no loss to the Lombards, so a loss of Rugiland to the Lombards by 493 is missing there.

region.text: Rugiland north of the Danube, left for the Feld and Pannonia

'the Langobards left and settled in a flat plain called Feld' (undated; the Little Alfold in Hungary); Cliopatria's Rugiland cells north of the Danube drop out of the Lombard shape in 546. Page silent on the year (confidence 1). Wacho page (read 2026-10-20): reign 'from an unknown date (perhaps c. 510) until his death in 539'; it says nothing of the move to Pannonia or the Feld. region.text: Pannonia, south and west of the Danube, 'Roman Pannonia'

ledger.note: 546: the Lombards move into Pannonia. 'Audouin led the Langobards into Roman Pannonia, south and west of the Danube' (Lombards page); 'He led the Lombards to Pannonia, where they were settled by Justinian I' (Audoin page); the Alboin page says they moved in 'while the Ostrogothic Kingdom was weakened' after 526 and puts Audoin on the throne about 547. No page dates the move (confidence 1); Cliopatria hands it over from the Ostrogothic Kingdom, and the Audoin page's 'settled by Justinian' would make the empire the counterpart instead. Wacho page (read 2026-10-20) is silent on Pannonia, so the move stays at Cliopatria's year.

region.text: the western Gepid lands between the Danube and the Tisza

ledger.note: 565: war with the Gepids breaks out again. 'Shortly, in 565, a new war erupted with the Gepids'; Justin II sent Baduarius (565 or 566) and the Lombards 'suffered a complete defeat'. The zone is the western Gepid land the Lombards hold in 567.
567: Alboin and the Avars destroy the Gepid kingdom. 'In 567 the allies made their final move against Cunimund.' Alboin killed the Gepid king and the Avars overran the Gepids.

567: the Lombards take the western Gepid lands. 'In 567 the allies made their final move against Cunimund' (Alboin page); the Avars 'demanded all of the lands held by the Gepids' after the war, and the Lombards kept them only until 568. The region is the overlap of Cliopatria's Lombard 567 and Gepid 566 shapes (110 cells).

region.text: Friuli, the Eastern Alps, Forum Iulii (Cividale)

2 April 568: the Lombards leave Pannonia to the Avars. 'The Lombard migration started on Easter Monday, 2 April 568'; 'the Avars were to take possession of Pannonia' and the Lombards could reclaim their former lands for 200 years if the Italian venture failed (the treaty is undated on the page, before 568).

'In 569, unopposed, he took northern Italy's main city, Milan'; by 570 'Alboin had taken their last defences in northern Italy' apart from the coast and some inland holdouts. The region is the Eastern Roman Empire dossier's own (the Po valley from Milan to Pavia and inland Tuscany) without Friuli, which is the 568 event above.

region.text: the Duchy of Tuscia, 65 cells of inland Tuscany

ledger.note: 577: the Duchy of Tuscia stands apart. 'Cleph ... completing the conquest of Tuscia' (574) and 'dukes ruled as absolute monarchs in their duchies' in the decade without a king (574-584); the page does not name Tuscia in 577. The year is Cliopatria's row start for the Duchy of Tuscia (confidence 1). Duchy of Tuscia page (read 2026-10-20): infobox 'Established: 576'; 'the first Lombard duchies formed after the death of King Alboin, during the period of ducal anarchy (about 574)'. The split stays at 577, the year of Cliopatria's Lombard and Tuscia shapes, a year after the page's 576.

wars.name: Lombard-Herulian war
wars.outcome: The Herulian kingdom, whose destruction 'modern date estimates' place between 493 and 511, was ended; the page gives no territorial change for the Lombards.
wars.note: 'in 494, Rodulf was pressured by his followers to attack the Lombards.' The pages opened give no month, place or border. Heruli page (read 2026-10-20): 'in 494, King Rodulf was pressured by his followers to attack the Lombards, despite their treaties'; 'Date estimates for the destruction of the kingdom have therefore ranged from 493-511'; no land or border is named, and the Feld sentence has no date.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid war (549-552)
wars.outcome: The Lombards 'defeated the Gepid leader Thurisind in 551 or 552 AD' at the Battle of Asfeld (552 on the Alboin and Audoin pages); Audoin also sent troops to Narses in Italy from 551. No border moved.
wars.note: 'In 552 the Langobards with a small amount of Roman support defeated the Gepids in a major battle.' Audoin inflicted 'a heavy defeat on the Gepids' the year he sent over 5,000 men against the Goths at Vesuvius.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid war (565-567)
wars.outcome: 'Alboin eventually destroyed the Gepid kingdom in 567 AD' with the Avars; the Lombards held the western Gepid lands until they left for Italy in 568.
wars.note: The Avar alliance dates to 566; 'The Avars demanded all of the lands held by the Gepids'.

wars.name: Lombard conquest of northern Italy

zones.text: the Po valley and inland Tuscany

wars.outcome: Friuli in 568, Milan on 3 September 569, the last northern defences by 570, Pavia in 572; Byzantine coastal cities and the Exarchate of Ravenna held out.
wars.note: The Kingdom of the Lombards page: the 'Exarchate of Ravenna and Duchy of Rome separated the northern Lombard duchies' from the southern; the Spoleto and Benevento duchies are undated on the pages and not in the Cliopatria shape.

wars.name: Frankish invasions of Lombard Italy
wars.outcome: Frankish raids on Burgundy from 569 or 570, a Frankish-Byzantine coalition of about 571, a Frankish invasion in 584, and 'In 585 he drove the Franks into modern Piedmont'; no border moved in the data.
wars.note: Autari 'repelled Frankish attacks, including in 588 and the 590s'. Clipped to the dossier's end (586) by the reviewer (eu-06-e); the later attacks belong to the successor dossier.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is recorded; the Danubian homelands are tribal, and in Italy the frontier with the Exarchate of Ravenna and Rome moved with each campaign and is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Lombards' 480-586 (ten shapes) covers the tribe in Scania and Central Europe and the kingdom in Pannonia and Italy to 586; its Kingdom of Italy row (587-1946, 48 shapes) continues the same Lombard kingdom to 774 and is for the owner of kingdom-of-italy to split; the Lombard kingdom 587-774 should be one dossier with this one (colour continuity, rule 2), or this dossier should name the split-off slug. Corrections: the 480 shape (Scania) and the 490 shape (a trail from Scania to the Danube) are wrong for the pages opened, which date nothing before Rugiland (after 487); the 480-487 Bardengau reading is confidence 1. Not on the pages opened: the date of the move from Rugiland to the Feld and Pannonia (Cliopatria 546; Audoin c. 547), the Heruli outcome, Noricum, the Spoleto and Benevento duchies (undated on the pages; they are Cliopatria rows of their own from 577, duchy-of-spoleto and duchy-of-benevento, outside the Lombard shape), the Moravian and Bohemian stay, and the origin of the 555 and 561 edge changes. Counterparts: the 488 Rugiland gain names kingdom-of-odoacer; the Rugiland dossier lists the Lombards as successor with no loss to them. The 546 Pannonia gain names ostrogothic-kingdom (Cliopatria's holder) at confidence 1, while the Audoin page has Justinian settling them. The Friuli 568 and Po valley 569 gains name the Eastern Roman Empire, whose dossier records one 569/9 loss that includes Friuli (this dossier splits Friuli into 568). The Avars take Pannonia in 568 (April) by treaty on the Alboin page. Gazetteer names needed: place Bardowick (Bardengau, 53.28 N 10.31 E); Cividale del Friuli and Pavia are not places in the gazetteer (Friuli-Venezia Giulia and the Pavia admin-1 are used). Page budget: five of five. Review fix 2026-10-20 (reviewer eu-06-e): (1) Syrmia with Sirmium (11 cells, 2,782 km2) is removed from the 555, 561 and 567 keyframes; it is Gepid to 567 (Cunimund page) and the Gepid dossier holds it. (2) The 480-487 location is now the Middle Danube (Lombards page: 'previously settled in the Middle Danube in the 5th century, near what is now Austria, Slovenia and Hungary'), drawn as a 110 km circle round Szombathely, with a 488 loss to nobody; the first draft's place Bardowick is dropped, so the gazetteer name is no longer needed. (3) The 488 Rugiland gain is confidence 2 (Heruli page 488, Odoacer page 'by 493'); eu-04's kingdom-of-odoacer still lacks the matching loss. (4) Pages opened for the thin findings: Wacho (silent on the move to Pannonia, which stays at confidence 1), Heruli (no land outcome), Duchy of Tuscia (established 576 against Cliopatria's 577). Budget: ten pages opened in all against five.
